title: Introduce epochal log tiling and cost-gradient alert smoother
author: Maya Chen
description:
Motivation: Recent incidents showed noisy long-tail log retention and spiky cost alerts that produced pager fatigue. This PR implements two complementary subsystems to reduce noise while preserving fidelity for root-cause: 1) epochal log tiling: a retention/compaction scheme that buckets invocation logs into time-anchored 'epochs' and keeps variable-fidelity tiles (high-fidelity for recent epochs, compacted digests for older epochs). 2) cost-gradient alert smoother: an adaptive alert thresholding algorithm that considers the short-term gradient of per-tenant token cost to suppress transient spikes and surface persistent regressions.

What this PR changes (summary): - New epochal tiler microservice (observability/log-tiler) with configurable epoch length and tile retention policy. - Retention controller that coordinates between object store (S3/GCS) and hot cache to keep recent tiles at full resolution. - Token-correlated lightweight phase metrics (metrics/token_phase_sampler) to enable low-cardinality attribution of where cost changes originate (prompt/response/kv-cache). - Cost-gradient alerting library (alerts/cost_gradient) with hysteresis and adaptive dampening; integrates into existing SLO pipeline. - New Grafana dashboard panels and an operator guide (docs/observability/epochal-tiling.md). - Unit and integration tests + upgrade notes.

Checklist: - [x] Design doc linked: https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-2418/epochal-log-tiling-and-cost-gradient-smoother - [x] Unit tests added - [x] Integration test in CI (observability smoke) - [x] Docs/ops runbook added - [x] Backwards-compatible: retention defaults preserve current retention windows unless operator flips the feature flag

Compatibility and rollout plan: This is feature-gated behind the runtime flag observability.epochal_tiling. Default is off in hosted. For Dedicated/Private customers runbook describes a staged rollout: enable on a small of tenants (10%) for two weeks, validate artifacts and SLOs, then scale. Cost-gradient smoother is opt-in per-tenant and exposes tuning knobs (window_length, slope_threshold, damping_factor).

Related work: ENG-2389 (prefetch sampler), PR #126712 (contextual log anchors) inspired decisions on digest formats. SUP-1221 documented a high-severity incident where noisy alerts obscured cost regressions.

Notes: The description intentionally avoids exposing internal S3 key formats; see docs/observability/epochal-tiling.md for operator-facing details.

changes_summary: Adds epochal log tiling and an adaptive cost-gradient smoother, plus dashboards and docs. Implements operator-safe defaults and feature flags to allow staged rollout. Introduces a low-cardinality token phase sampler to help pinpoint whether cost slope changes stem from prompt length, generation length, or KV cache misses.
review_comments: Ethan Park: Can we make the default epoch length conservative (30m) in hosted to avoid retention blowups? Also requested that tiler metrics expose per-epoch bytes written so we can monitor the compaction ratio.
Maya Chen: Responded - set hosted default to 30m and added tile_bytes_written metric (+dashboard sparkline).
Rita Gomez: Requested unit tests around edge-case where epoch boundary moves during long-running invocation; suggested adding a deterministic boundary cut test.
Maya Chen: Added deterministic boundary unit test and an e2e integration test that replays long prompts across epoch boundaries.
Liam O'Neill: Approved after CI green and docs updated — noted one minor style nit in smoother.py (renamed variable to damping_factor).
release_notes: Introduce epochal log tiling (configurable, feature-gated) to reduce long-term log storage costs while preserving high-fidelity recent logs. Add cost-gradient alert smoothing to reduce alert noise for transient token-cost spikes. New dashboard panels and operator runbook included.
backout_plan: Feature flags allow immediate disable of epochal tiling and smoother. If unexpected retention regressions occur, operators should flip observability.epochal_tiling=false and run backfill/rehydrate job as described in docs/observability/epochal-tiling.md.
upgrade_notes: Dedicated/Private: ensure object-store lifecycle policies are compatible; migrations are non-destructive by default. Hosted: rollout handled by platform ops. See docs/observability/epochal-tiling.md for tenant-level knobs.
notes_for_reviewers: Focus reviews on: 1) retention controller failure modes (controller.go), 2) smoother tuning defaults and unit tests (alerts/cost_gradient/smoother.py), 3) dashboard queries for tile_bytes_written and compact_ratio. Perf impact on hot path is minimal; token_phase_sampler is sampled at 0.1% by default.
